what_it_does: FPGAs (field-programmable gate arrays) are chips whose internal wiring can be reconfigured after manufacture, making them useful for running many different tasks on shared hardware. The problem is that when multiple users share one FPGA, the system only supports running completely independent jobs — it cannot chain tasks together so the output of one feeds directly into the next like an assembly line. Nyx solves this by splitting the FPGA into separate reconfigurable zones and introducing 'virtual FIFOs' — software-managed holding buffers that temporarily store data flowing between chained tasks, so each task can run whenever its zone is free without waiting for neighboring tasks to be running at the same moment. A managing program (the hypervisor) tracks what data is waiting where and schedules each task across zones at high throughput, enabling assembly-line (dataflow) pipelines on shared hardware for the first time.
